The hazard index is joined from `public.tract_risk` — FEMA's National Risk Index, covering 85,154 tracts — matched to properties by Census tract, and in the v254 dry run (Oct 21, 2026, read-only) it filled 137,927 records, lifting coverage from 65.3% to 88.7% [S1].

The measured post-run figure was slightly higher, 88.8% across 587,787 records, and the record count matched the dry run exactly [S1]. Remaining gaps are properties without a tract geocode; the documentation puts the ceiling at roughly 84.6% tract coverage before the county-FIPS step, so the join effectively exhausted the tract-linked population [S3].

Two caveats worth noting: the join fills NULLs only and records its method per row, and updating that input column re-queues affected rows for v43 rescoring, so scores move once the queue drains [S1]. Hazard is a medium-weight input in the score (default 40 where missing) [S6]. For actual per-property hazard values, check the Spain Terminal.
